---
title: "Fundamentals: eight development frameworks, made clickable, with the Indian evidence"
category: "Announcements"
---
The frameworks that development work runs on are usually taught as a diagram on a slide. [Fundamentals](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/) draws each one so you can click it, and attaches the Indian evidence to every position on it.

Eight pages, all free, no sign-in:

- **[The Indian Wheel of Power & Powerlessness](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/wheel.html)** — twelve axes and 36 bands, each position backed by NFHS-5, PLFS, Census 2011, NCRB, AISHE or the NSS. The wheel itself is by The Listeners Collective.
- **[Arnstein's Ladder of Citizen Participation](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/ladder.html)** — the 1969 ladder with the Indian law, scheme or judgment sitting on each of its eight rungs, from Niyamgiri's gram sabha referendum down to consultations held after the decision was taken.
- **[Gaventa's Power Cube](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/power-cube.html)** — spaces, levels and forms of power, with evidence for all nine categories and eight documented Indian cases plotted on all three dimensions.
- **[The Capability Approach](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/capabilities.html)** — Sen's argument followed through seven resources, from what a programme provides to what a person can actually do with it. School places against reading levels; toilets built against toilets used.
- **[Practical and Strategic Gender Needs](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/gender-needs.html)** — Moser's distinction, with twelve Indian interventions plotted by how much each lightens a woman's day and how far it moves the division of labour.
- **[The Sustainable Livelihoods Framework](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/livelihoods.html)** — eight Indian livelihoods drawn as asset pentagons across human, social, natural, physical and financial capital, so the shapes can be compared side by side.
- **[The Social Model of Disability](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/social-model.html)** — six Indian outcomes drawn as stacks of attitudinal, environmental, institutional and communication barriers standing between a person and a school, a job, a bus, a public building.
- **[Who Counts](https://www.impactmojo.in/fundamentals/who-counts.html)** — eight gaps in India's official statistics, whether never asked, counted badly or frozen, with what each gap costs and the closest available substitute.

Every number on every page carries its source. Where the evidence is thin or contested, the page says so rather than rounding it off.

Works on a phone, in dark or light theme, and offline once you have opened it.
